text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- High education council meets to chart a reform strategy to overhaul the education and research system.
- Authorities raise minimum wage by 50 percent, to be implemented in three stages starting in May.

- Resumption of flights by Air Algerie to Paris upsets British Airways. The British airline said on Saturday it had diverted some flights away from Charles de Gaulle airport after French authorities allowed Air Algerie to resume operations there. Air Algerie has stopped services to Paris since 1995 in a security row with the French authorities.
- British Airways wants to practise "apartheid" at Roissy Charles de Gaulle airport.
- The U.S. revise their policy towards "terrorism" after massacres of civilians in Algeria blamed by the authorities there on Moslem militants.

- Abdelkader Bensalah, head of the National Democratic Rally (RND) party, says he hopes all political parties will adopt a code of good conduct during the June 5 parliamentary elections. The RND, formed less than two months ago, groups President Liamine Zeoual's political backers.
- Abdelkader Bensalah says his RND party will be the main political force in the upcoming parliament.

- Seventeen political parties excluded from the independent committeee to supervise elections for falling short of the minimum number of candidates to the 380-seat National Assembley. The law states that party should have more than 12 candidates to claim representation on the poll watchdog.

- Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, now personal envoy of the U.N. Secretary-General, to visit Polisario rear base in southwestern Algeria on Sunday to try to tackle U.N. stalled peace plan in the Western Sahara.
